cardSummary: Shows how recent emails, events and sales activity contributed to enquiries, placements and revenue.
title: Salesforce Multi-Touch Attribution and Revenue Reporting
ownership: I identified the attribution gap and owned the architecture, Flow design, scoring rules, release and later refinements.
adoption: The model is live in Salesforce and supplies an ROI snapshot for resource decisions.
summary: I built a weighted Salesforce model that traces recent email, event, sales and organisational activity through to enquiries, referrals, opportunities and placements.
details: Three Salesforce Flow paths handle Lead enquiries, Contact enquiries and Account-level referrals. The calculation uses a three-week activity window, Campaign membership, recognised domains, MAT and Account context, returning-customer status and the order of each touchpoint. Every applicable result is normalised to 100% and stored in a custom Attribution Model record for dashboards and revenue reporting.
featuredMetric: Every result totals 100%, giving teams a live comparison of channel influence.

cardSummary: Puts organisations, contracts and local-authority pricing into one usable Salesforce hierarchy.
title: Local-Authority Account Hierarchy, Contract Pricing and Commercial Risk
ownership: I made the case for the model, then handled its design, automation, validation, release and upkeep.
adoption: It is now the production structure for Local Authority relationships, pricing, segmentation and reporting.
summary: I reorganised Salesforce around Local Authorities so users could see the organisations, people, contracts, prices and commercial exposure linked to each one.
details: The new hierarchy replaced a series of one-to-one views with an account-level picture of every client in a Local Authority area. Custom Metadata Types, Salesforce Flow and validation rules keep Accounts, Leads and Contacts aligned. Contract and Opportunity automation also shows users the right bespoke charge rate and highlights authority-level risk.
featuredMetric: Covers 200+ Local Authorities, 1,000+ Accounts and 20,000+ Leads and Contacts.

cardSummary: Shows schools as part of their wider MAT or governing organisation in Salesforce and MCAE.
title: MAT and Private Governing-Organisation Commercial Architecture
ownership: I defined the commercial model, worked out the Salesforce architecture and presented the case for senior approval.
adoption: The Director and CEO approved it. The model now informs email marketing and account strategy.
summary: I mapped schools to their MATs, independent-school groups and other governing bodies, then carried those relationships into Salesforce and MCAE.
details: Additional parent structures hold each school's governing context, while custom lookup keys preserve it on Leads before conversion. One dynamic Screen Flow works across several record types. Validation rules and exact or wildcard domain matching keep the structure accurate. When one organisation buys, Salesforce Campaigns can flag related records for MCAE validation, grading, nurture and sales follow-up.
featuredMetric: Mapped roughly half of the school Accounts to 215 MATs and other governing organisations.

cardSummary: Gives sales a guided Lead workflow, a forecast value and an automatic 21-day close rule.
title: Salesforce Lead Opportunity Forecasting and Automated Closure
ownership: I spotted the process gap and took the solution through design, build, release and live refinement.
adoption: The workflow is in production and keeps a reportable history of repeated sales attempts.
summary: I created an opportunity process that works before Lead conversion, calculates a forecast value, keeps previous attempts and closes inactive work automatically.
details: A Salesforce Screen Flow takes users through identification, outreach, response and outcome. Forecast value draws on the previous 12 months of purchasing data, including organisation type, rate, weekly hours, service duration and MAT context. A custom object stores each attempt while the Lead shows the current one. If nobody updates it for 21 days, scheduled automation closes the attempt and records why.
featuredMetric: Uses 12 months of purchase data and closes inactive Lead opportunities after 21 days.

cardSummary: Makes new Salesforce features usable without giving people access they do not need.
title: Salesforce Access Governance, Data Standards and User Adoption
ownership: As the departmental Salesforce super user, I owned the features and adjusted them in response to user feedback.
adoption: More than 30 staff can use the production features; Development and Referrals use them most often.
summary: I managed access to Salesforce objects, fields and Flows, improved CRM data standards and helped staff adopt new features through testing, training and support.
details: I configured permission sets, object permissions, field-level access and validation rules for custom features. I also standardised Lead, Contact and Account data, tested releases under different access levels and dealt with user issues. Documentation, training and coaching translated the configuration into day-to-day working instructions for more than 30 users.
featuredMetric: Production features are available to 30+ users with access matched to their roles.

cardSummary: Gave sales, marketing and operations one model for account relationships and follow-up.
title: Commercial Systems Operating Model and Change Leadership
ownership: I developed the relationship-led operating model and presented it over several senior-leadership meetings.
adoption: It passed the formal approval process, first with the Director and then the CEO.
summary: I gave sales, marketing, client services and operations a shared way to understand account relationships, ownership and follow-up.
details: After securing Director and CEO approval, I put the model into Salesforce and MCAE through new workflows, checkpoints and responsibilities. Documentation, training and user feedback helped it settle into daily work. It changed how the company thought about related Accounts and influenced both email marketing and the wider brand voice.
featuredMetric: Won Director and CEO approval and moved the model into company use.

cardSummary: Cleaned the legacy database and rebuilt marketing automation in MCAE.
title: Mailchimp-to-MCAE Migration, Data Remediation and Platform Rebuild
ownership: I led the data clean-up, platform design, migration controls, testing and production launch.
adoption: The rebuilt instance now underpins the company's MCAE audiences and campaign work.
summary: I moved the organisation out of a high-risk Mailchimp and Pro-Net setup and built most of its MCAE instance from scratch.
details: Before migrating anything, I reviewed duplicates, consent risk, poor-quality records and data that was no longer usable. Viable prospects moved into MCAE. I then set up the Salesforce link, audience rules, consent and suppression controls, preferences, send hygiene and repeatable campaign processes needed for production use.
featuredMetric: Reduced 30,000 legacy contacts to about 19,000 viable prospects; successful sends reached roughly 99%.

cardSummary: Uses live rules to decide who qualifies, who is suppressed and which records need repair.
title: Initial MCAE Audience, Consent and Suppression Architecture
ownership: I designed the original list strategy and set up its suppression, repair and preference rules.
adoption: Completed in January 2026, it remains the production base for three commercial audiences.
summary: I built MCAE audience rules that respond when a prospect's data, permission, subscription or activity changes.
details: The architecture contains about 400 MCAE lists. Dynamic lists represent a prospect's current state; static micro-segmentation lists retain past actions. The Master Suppression List, preference and unsubscribe controls, missing-data routes and merge-tag checks decide who can be emailed. Three audience models cover provision and services, community influence and professional development.
featuredMetric: About 400 MCAE lists manage three audiences and their changing permission states.

cardSummary: Lets old signals expire, records requalify and uncertain cases go to a person for review.
title: Ongoing MCAE Audience Governance and Predictive Qualification
ownership: Since launch, I have monitored the production architecture and extended its qualification rules.
adoption: It is live for audience eligibility, buyer qualification, exception review and re-engagement.
summary: I maintain the MCAE audience system so qualification can change, old activity can expire and unresolved data can be checked by a person.
details: Since February 2026, I have refined the rules for qualification, suppression, repair, subscriptions and Salesforce-based segmentation. Scores now reset after set periods, profiles can degrade and sub-profiles separate different kinds of fit. Known, inferred and unknown states expose uncertainty. Administrator queues and proof-of-life journeys deal with cases automation should not decide alone.
featuredMetric: Qualification can reverse, scores can expire and uncertain records reach a human reviewer.

cardSummary: Tracks campaign performance and revenue while carrying one audience from Mailchimp into MCAE.
title: Email Campaign Operations Across Mailchimp and MCAE
ownership: I was the sole owner of campaign operations and set the order of Pardot/MCAE work that could affect the channel.
adoption: The channel remained live while the same audience moved from Mailchimp to MCAE.
summary: I ran campaigns in Mailchimp and later MCAE, protecting continuity during the Salesforce transition and making the results easier to trace commercially.
details: I planned, produced and measured more than 50 campaigns involving email, events, webinars and gated content. The internal model associated Mailchimp activity with about £419,475 of revenue influence in 2025. After the audience moved to MCAE, average open rate rose from about 8% to 40%, the best campaign reached 84%, and £127,642.98 of realised revenue was attributed to MCAE activity from February to May 2026.
featuredMetric: £127.6k in realised revenue was attributed to MCAE activity from February to May 2026.

cardSummary: Replaced lost Mailchimp content blocks with reusable, tested XHTML modules for MCAE.
title: Modular MCAE XHTML Email Template System
ownership: I designed, tested and documented the system, directed the AI-assisted XHTML work and trained its users.
adoption: It became the organisation's standard system for producing marketing emails.
summary: When the move from Mailchimp removed the old drag-and-drop blocks, I created a modular XHTML system for MCAE.
details: I reviewed the Mailchimp layouts tied to the strongest commercial results and broke their recurring patterns into reusable MCAE modules. AI assisted with XHTML generation, but I set the requirements, reviewed the code and tested it in Gmail and Outlook. Documentation and training let non-coders use the templates. The library grew as new campaign needs appeared.
featuredMetric: About 13 modules across 13 templates cut a typical email build from several days to roughly one.

cardSummary: Prepared CRM data and automations for a future AI layer that was designed but never funded.
title: AI-Ready Salesforce, Pardot and Website-Automation Architecture
ownership: I built the data and automation foundations and documented the unfunded AI layer separately.
adoption: The CRM, Campaign and automation work is live. The proposed AI execution layer is not.
summary: I prepared Salesforce and Pardot/MCAE data, Campaigns, segmentation and website handoffs for possible future AI-assisted workflows.
details: Structured Lead and Contact fields, Campaign links and journey rules give a future agent defined commercial context to work with. Zapier already passes website activity and form submissions into Pardot/MCAE. I also specified an AI enhancement for the attribution model, but funding for the required tokens was withdrawn before any model, agent or AI-driven attribution was deployed.
featuredMetric: The AI-ready foundations are live; no AI model or agent was deployed.

cardSummary: Brings Local Authority relationships, pricing and bid evidence into one Salesforce decision screen.
title: Local-Authority Commercial Intelligence Application
ownership: I owned the problem definition, scoring rules, build direction, release and live refinements.
adoption: The production app is used for pricing, relationship management and bid prioritisation.
summary: I created a Salesforce app that puts Local Authority, Account, Contract and Bid information on one decision screen.
details: I defined the requirements, data relationships, scoring rules and user flow. The app brings together Local Authorities, Accounts, Bids, Referrals, Contracts and custom prices. AI assisted with Apex and component development; I reviewed, tested and validated the output. Users can now see one-to-many relationships, find the correct charge rate and compare bid results before deciding where to spend limited time.
featuredMetric: Used for decisions involving 200+ Local Authorities, 1,000+ Accounts and about 2,500 Bids a year.

cardSummary: Adds a small monthly challenge to the newsletter without storing names or email addresses.
title: AI-Assisted Newsletter Engagement and Privacy-Conscious Leaderboard
ownership: I came up with the product and owned its requirements, AI-assisted build, testing and release.
adoption: It is live in the Fresh Start newsletter and available through a free subscription.
summary: I made a monthly newsletter game with an anonymous leaderboard and no need to retain personal user data.
details: Structured prompts produced the first working version, which I tested, debugged and refined over three major iterations. The app uses available five-letter display names and monthly ranking logic without storing participants' names or email addresses. GitHub holds the project and Vercel hosts the live version used in the newsletter.
featuredMetric: A working prototype took one day; the refined product was live about a week later.

cardSummary: Tests how trust moves through communities, then applies the findings to strategy and MCAE writing.
title: Community Strategy Framework and MCAE Thought Leadership
ownership: I founded the venture and researched, wrote and published its frameworks, with guidance from a mentor and adviser.
adoption: The work is published on the maintained DCC website and informs my employed systems work at Fresh Start in Education.
summary: I developed a five-stage community funnel and a community taxonomy, then published the research alongside practical MCAE papers.
details: I compared more than 20 community-funnel models and interviewed a financial representative with over 20 years of experience. The result was a five-stage model: Awareness, Interaction, Engagement, Buy-In and Advocacy, with trust and quality present throughout. A second framework covers close, broad, digital and product communities. I published seven community-strategy blogs and four MCAE papers, then used reader response to refine the work.
featuredMetric: Seven community blogs and four MCAE papers, informed by 20+ model reviews and an expert interview.

cardSummary: Carries event invitations, registrations, attendance and follow-up through MCAE and Salesforce.
title: Webinar and Event Registration, CRM and Follow-Up Automation
ownership: I owned the route from registration to follow-up across campaigns, Salesforce and MCAE.
adoption: The workflow is used for events, webinars and audience-specific follow-up.
summary: I linked event and webinar invitations, registrations, attendance and follow-up through Salesforce Campaigns and MCAE.
details: The workflow records the journey from invitation and registration to attendance, Salesforce Campaign membership and the right follow-up in MCAE. Participation remains visible in the CRM and contributes to event-influence reporting. My delivery included email activity and live Zoom operation or hosting, not presenting the webinar content.
featuredMetric: Covered email activity for 8 events and 2 webinars, plus live Zoom operation or hosting.

cardSummary: Rebuilt a stalled youth programme while growing attendance and cutting annual spend.
title: Youth Programme Revitalisation, Audience Growth and Cost Control
ownership: I owned the event plan, programme delivery, marketing, volunteer development and departmental budget.
adoption: This was the department's way of working across in-person, digital and hybrid programmes from 2022 to February 2024.
summary: I restarted youth events and community programmes by changing the programme, promotion, partnerships and day-to-day operation.
details: I reviewed the event portfolio, improved its consistency and used grassroots promotion to rebuild participation. Relationships with young people, families and partner organisations shaped the programme. I led 10 established volunteers on rotation and recruited and trained nine junior volunteers. Better planning and budget control helped the growth last beyond a single event.
featuredMetric: Tripled recurring attendance, doubled community membership and cut annual departmental spending by 30%.

cardSummary: Moved from team member to operational leadership on week-long conferences for 30,000+ people.
title: Large-Scale International Conference Operations and Volunteer Leadership
ownership: During the internship I progressed from team member to co-manager and then the internally titled Event Operations Manager.
adoption: I held broad delegated authority, with six regular direct reports and peak oversight of about 450 people through team leaders.
summary: I planned and ran conference operations involving access, volunteers, participant services, VIP areas and live risk response.
details: I joined as an Operations Team Member in 2017, became Operations Co-Manager in 2018 and held the internally titled Event Operations Manager role from 2019 to July 2021. I managed about six regular direct reports and roughly 20 changing reporting relationships during conferences. At peak, I oversaw about 450 people through their team leaders as part of the conference lead's right-hand team.
featuredMetric: Conference operations for 30,000+ attendees, with peak oversight of about 450 people through team leaders.
